title: Jeremiah Chapter 22 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 22 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 22 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 22.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 22, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Go down to the house of the king of Judah
Weep ye not for the dead
And many nations shall pass by this city
questions.correctAnswer: Go down to the house of the king of Judah
questions.explanation: This command appears first as it is stated in the very first verse of the chapter.

questions.question: What does the LORD ask the king of Judah to do in Jeremiah 22?
questions.correctAnswer: Execute judgment and righteousness
questions.explanation: The LORD commands the king to execute judgment and righteousness in Jeremiah 22:3.

questions.question: What shall happen if the king of Judah does not hear these words?
options: The house shall become a desolation
Kings shall enter in by the gates
The city shall be a wilderness
questions.correctAnswer: The house shall become a desolation
questions.explanation: The LORD states that if they do not heed the words, the house will become a desolation in Jeremiah 22:5.

questions.question: What metaphor does the LORD use to describe the king's house of Judah?
options: Gilead and the head of Lebanon
questions.correctAnswer: Gilead and the head of Lebanon
questions.explanation: The LORD refers to the king's house as Gilead and the head of Lebanon in Jeremiah 22:6.

questions.question: What will happen to the choice cedars mentioned in Jeremiah 22?
options: They will be cut down and cast into the fire
They will be used for building
They will grow tall and strong
questions.correctAnswer: They will be cut down and cast into the fire
questions.explanation: The verse states that destroyers will cut down the choice cedars and cast them into the fire in Jeremiah 22:7.

questions.question: What will many nations say about the city?
options: Wherefore hath the LORD done thus unto this great city?
questions.correctAnswer: Wherefore hath the LORD done thus unto this great city?
questions.explanation: This question is posed by many nations passing by the city in Jeremiah 22:8.

questions.question: Why will the nations answer about the city?
options: Because they have forsaken the covenant of the LORD
Because they have built great walls
questions.correctAnswer: Because they have forsaken the covenant of the LORD
questions.explanation: The nations will answer this because they have forsaken the covenant and worshiped other gods as stated in Jeremiah 22:9.

questions.question: Who should weep sore according to Jeremiah 22?
questions.correctAnswer: Him that goeth away
questions.explanation: The verse instructs to weep sore for him that goeth away as he shall return no more in Jeremiah 22:10.

questions.question: What does the LORD say about the fatherless and the widow?
questions.correctAnswer: Do no wrong to them
questions.explanation: The text instructs to do no wrong to the stranger, the fatherless, nor the widow in Jeremiah 22:3.

questions.question: What does the LORD swear by if the king does not listen?
questions.correctAnswer: By Himself
questions.explanation: The LORD swears by Himself in Jeremiah 22:5.

questions.question: What is the condition for kings to enter by the gates of this house?
options: They must execute judgment and righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: They must execute judgment and righteousness
questions.explanation: If they execute judgment and righteousness, kings will enter by the gates as stated in Jeremiah 22:4.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD commands the king to deliver the spoiled out of the hand of the oppressor.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: This is true as stated in Jeremiah 22:3.

questions.question: True or False: The king of Judah is referred to as the head of Egypt.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: This is false; he is referred to as Gilead and the head of Lebanon in Jeremiah 22:6.

questions.question: True or False: The city mentioned in Jeremiah 22 is described as great.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text does not describe the city as great; it says 'this great city' in the context of questioning why the LORD has acted thus, indicating past grandeur.

questions.question: True or False: The text encourages weeping for the dead.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text advises not to weep for the dead but to weep for him that goeth away in Jeremiah 22:10.

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 22 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 22 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What will happen to Shallum, the son of Josiah, according to Jeremiah 22:11?
options: He shall not return thither any more.
He will become a great king.
He will lead the people in worship.
questions.correctAnswer: He shall not return thither any more.
questions.explanation: The verse states that Shallum will not return to the place he left, signifying his exile and judgment from the Lord. (Jeremiah 22:11)

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 22:4 promise will happen if judgment and righteousness are executed?
options: Kings will enter through the gates riding in chariots.
There will be no inhabitants left.
questions.correctAnswer: Kings will enter through the gates riding in chariots.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:4 promises that if judgment and righteousness are executed, kings will enter the house riding in chariots, indicating blessings for obedience.

questions.question: What is said to be the consequence for those who build their houses by unrighteousness?
options: Woe unto him that buildeth his house by unrighteousness.
They will be favored by the king.
questions.correctAnswer: Woe unto him that buildeth his house by unrighteousness.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:13 pronounces woe upon those who build their houses through unrighteous means, indicating God's disapproval.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 22:12 indicate about Shallum's fate?
options: He will return to his homeland.
He shall die in the place whither they have led him captive.
He will be restored to his throne.
He will be remembered as a great leader.
questions.correctAnswer: He shall die in the place whither they have led him captive.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:12 clearly states that Shallum will die in captivity, emphasizing the consequences of his actions.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 22:15, what was required for King Josiah to do well?
options: He ate and drank, and did judgment and justice.
questions.correctAnswer: He ate and drank, and did judgment and justice.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:15 indicates that it was King Josiah's commitment to judgment and justice that led to his well-being.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 22:16 suggest is necessary to know the Lord?
options: Judging the cause of the poor and needy.
questions.correctAnswer: Judging the cause of the poor and needy.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:16 suggests that knowing the Lord involves caring for the poor and needy, reflecting His character.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 22:17 say about the eyes and heart of the king?
options: They are for covetousness, oppression, and violence.
They seek the welfare of the people.
questions.correctAnswer: They are for covetousness, oppression, and violence.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:17 reveals that the king's eyes and heart are directed towards selfish desires and wrongdoing, which displeases God.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 22:18 say about the lamentations for Jehoiakim?
options: They will lament greatly for him.
They shall not lament for him.
He will be honored after death.
questions.correctAnswer: They shall not lament for him.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:18 states that there will be no lament for Jehoiakim, indicating his rejection by the people due to his actions.

questions.question: What type of burial is foretold for Jehoiakim in Jeremiah 22:19?
options: He shall be buried with honor.
He shall be buried with the burial of an ass.
He will be buried in a royal tomb.
He shall have a grand funeral.
questions.correctAnswer: He shall be buried with the burial of an ass.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:19 describes Jehoiakim's burial as disgraceful, likening it to that of an ass, emphasizing his dishonor.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 22:20 instruct to do as a response to the destruction of the lovers?
options: To go up to Lebanon and cry.
questions.correctAnswer: To go up to Lebanon and cry.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:20 instructs to cry out due to the destruction of the lovers, reflecting the sorrow over lost alliances.

questions.question: What is a key lesson from Jeremiah 22:13 regarding fair treatment of workers?
options: One should exploit workers for profit.
All workers should be paid fairly for their service.
Workers should be grateful for any payment.
questions.correctAnswer: All workers should be paid fairly for their service.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:13 emphasizes the importance of treating workers justly and paying them for their work, reflecting God's justice.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 22:10, who is advised not to weep for the dead?
questions.correctAnswer: The people.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:10 instructs the people not to weep for the dead but rather for those who go away, indicating the seriousness of exile.

questions.question: Is it true that God promises prosperity to those who act unjustly according to Jeremiah 22:13?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:13 indicates that building by unrighteousness brings woe, not prosperity.

questions.question: Is it true that the king's house is compared to a wilderness in Jeremiah 22:6?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:6 compares the king's house to a wilderness, indicating God's judgment over disobedience.

questions.question: Is it true that Jeremiah 22:4 encourages doing violence to the stranger?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:3 explicitly commands not to do violence to the stranger, emphasizing justice.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 22 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 22.

questions.question: What did God say would happen to Coniah, the son of Jehoiakim?
questions.correctAnswer: He will be cast out
questions.explanation: God declares He will cast Coniah out into another country where he was not born (Jeremiah 22:26).

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 22:21, what was the response of the people when God spoke to them in prosperity?
options: They said, I will not hear
questions.correctAnswer: They said, I will not hear
questions.explanation: The verse states that the people responded, 'I will not hear,' indicating their refusal to listen to God's words (Jeremiah 22:21).

questions.question: What shall happen to all the pastors and lovers mentioned in Jeremiah 22:22?
questions.correctAnswer: They will go into captivity
questions.explanation: The wind shall eat up all the pastors, and their lovers shall go into captivity as a consequence of their wickedness (Jeremiah 22:22).

questions.question: What metaphor is used in Jeremiah 22:23 to describe the pain that will come upon the inhabitants of Lebanon?
options: Pangs of a woman in travail
questions.correctAnswer: Pangs of a woman in travail
questions.explanation: The verse uses the metaphor of the pangs of a woman in travail to illustrate the impending pain and distress (Jeremiah 22:23).

questions.question: What does God compare the king's house of Judah to in Jeremiah 22:6?
questions.correctAnswer: A wilderness
questions.explanation: God compares the king's house of Judah to Gilead and Lebanon but states that He will make it a wilderness (Jeremiah 22:6).

questions.question: What is God's declaration about Coniah in Jeremiah 22:30?
options: He will be a great ruler
questions.correctAnswer: He will be written childless
questions.explanation: God commands to write Coniah as childless, stating that no man of his seed shall prosper (Jeremiah 22:30).

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'Coniah' mean in Jeremiah 22:24?
questions.correctAnswer: God is gracious
questions.explanation: The name Coniah means 'Yahweh has established,' which reflects God's sovereignty despite the king's failures (Jeremiah 22:24).

questions.question: What literary device is used in Jeremiah 22:29 with the phrase 'O earth, earth, earth'?
questions.correctAnswer: Anaphora
questions.explanation: The repetition of 'earth' is an example of anaphora, emphasizing the gravity of the message (Jeremiah 22:29).

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of judgment against disobedience found in Jeremiah 22:9?
questions.correctAnswer: Ezekiel 18:30
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:30 calls for repentance from all offenses, echoing the judgment theme in Jeremiah 22:9 where the people forsake the covenant.

questions.question: Which passage in Revelation reflects the consequences of disobedience similar to Jeremiah 22:25?
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation 21:8
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:8 lists consequences for the disobedient, paralleling the warning given in Jeremiah 22:25 about judgment.

questions.question: What comes before Jeremiah 22:21?
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah 22:20
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:20 precedes verse 21 and discusses the destruction of the lovers, leading into the lament of the people (Jeremiah 22:20).

questions.question: What theme from Jeremiah 22:22 also appears in Isaiah 57:20?
questions.correctAnswer: Captivity of the wicked
questions.explanation: Both passages discuss the fate of the wicked who will face judgment and captivity, reflecting God's consistent theme of justice (Jeremiah 22:22).

questions.question: The punishment of Coniah in Jeremiah 22:30 signifies what about his lineage?
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be cut off
questions.explanation: The declaration that no man of Coniah's seed shall prosper indicates the cutting off of his lineage from ruling (Jeremiah 22:30).

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 22:30 states that Coniah shall prosper sitting upon the throne of David.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:30 explicitly states that no man of Coniah's seed shall prosper, indicating the opposite of prosperity.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 22:27 indicates that the people will return to the land they desire.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:27 states that they shall not return to the land they desire, indicating a permanent consequence for their actions.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 22 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 22 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Jeremiah 22:3 teach about God's expectation for human justice?
options: God commands the execution of judgment and righteousness, protecting the oppressed and vulnerable
God is indifferent to social justice and focuses only on ritual obedience
God requires worship only, without regard to ethical treatment of others
God permits injustice if it benefits the king and his servants
questions.correctAnswer: God commands the execution of judgment and righteousness, protecting the oppressed and vulnerable
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:3 explicitly commands executing judgment and righteousness, delivering the spoiled from oppressors, and protecting strangers, orphans, and widows, showing God's concern for justice.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine judgment is taught in Jeremiah 22:5?
options: Disobedience to God's command leads to desolation of the king’s house
God will always preserve the king’s house regardless of sin
God’s judgment is delayed indefinitely to allow repentance
Desolation occurs only due to foreign invasion, not divine will
questions.correctAnswer: Disobedience to God's command leads to desolation of the king’s house
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:5 declares God’s oath that if the king does not heed His words, the house will become desolate, demonstrating the certainty of divine judgment on disobedience.

questions.question: What doctrine about covenant unfaithfulness and idolatry does Jeremiah 22:9 teach?
options: Forsaking the covenant and worshipping other gods brings divine judgment
Idolatry is tolerated if it brings peace
The covenant is conditional and can be replaced by new agreements
Worship of other gods is irrelevant to God’s judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Forsaking the covenant and worshipping other gods brings divine judgment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:9 explains that the reason for God's judgment is the people forsaking the covenant and serving other gods, showing the seriousness of covenant violation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Jeremiah 22:24 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:24 shows God's sovereign authority by declaring that even if Coniah were a signet on His right hand, God would still remove him, emphasizing divine control over kings.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Jeremiah 22:16 regarding God's character?
questions.correctAnswer: Righteousness
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:16 emphasizes God's righteousness as He judges the cause of the poor and needy, showing that justice is central to His nature.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 22:30 connect to the broader biblical narrative of Davidic kingship?
options: It declares the permanent end of Coniah’s line on the throne, preparing for the messianic hope beyond David’s descendants
It affirms Coniah’s eternal dynasty as unbreakable
It predicts the restoration of all Davidic kings through human effort
It denies any future kingship after Josiah without divine intervention
questions.correctAnswer: It declares the permanent end of Coniah’s line on the throne, preparing for the messianic hope beyond David’s descendants
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:30 proclaims that no descendant of Coniah will prosper on David’s throne, pointing to the need for a messianic king beyond this corrupted lineage (cf. Jeremiah 23:5).

questions.question: In what way does Jeremiah 22:10 anticipate themes of exile and loss found elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It mourns the irrevocable departure from the homeland, paralleling Israel’s exile in Babylon
It celebrates the return of exiles to their land
It promises immediate restoration without judgment
It denies the reality of exile as permanent
questions.correctAnswer: It mourns the irrevocable departure from the homeland, paralleling Israel’s exile in Babylon
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:10 warns that those who leave will never return, foreshadowing the exile theme central to the prophetic literature and Israel’s history.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 22:13 and 22:17 teach about social sin and divine judgment?
options: Unrighteous economic practices and shedding innocent blood provoke God’s judgment
Social sins are secondary to ritual failures
Economic injustice is unrelated to divine judgment
Violence is permitted if it advances political power
questions.correctAnswer: Unrighteous economic practices and shedding innocent blood provoke God’s judgment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:13 condemns building wealth by unrighteousness and unpaid labor, while 22:17 highlights covetousness and violence as reasons for judgment, showing God’s concern for social justice.

questions.question: What theological insight arises from synthesizing Jeremiah 22:6 and 22:7 about God's judgment?
options: God’s judgment transforms places of strength into desolation through destruction
God’s judgment is only symbolic and not physical
God spares the strong and only punishes the weak
God’s judgment is reversible at human will
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment transforms places of strength into desolation through destruction
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:6 compares the king’s house to strong regions (Gilead, Lebanon), while 22:7 speaks of destroyers cutting down cedars, illustrating how God brings desolation to what was once strong.

questions.question: What doctrinal synthesis is taught by Jeremiah 22:25 and 22:26 regarding exile and divine justice?
options: Exile is a divinely ordained punishment involving removal from the land and death in a foreign country
Exile is a human mistake, not divinely sanctioned
God promises eventual restoration without judgment
Exile is permanent with no hope of return
questions.correctAnswer: Exile is a divinely ordained punishment involving removal from the land and death in a foreign country
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:25-26 details how God will deliver Coniah and his mother into captivity and death in a foreign land, demonstrating exile as divine judgment.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Jeremiah 22:24-30 unjustly condemns Coniah’s lineage without hope. What does this passage actually teach?
options: God pronounces a specific curse on Coniah’s descendants, preventing them from ruling on David’s throne
God offers Coniah’s line a chance to repent and regain the throne
The passage encourages political rebellion against Coniah
The lineage is condemned due to foreign political pressure, not divine decree
questions.correctAnswer: God pronounces a specific curse on Coniah’s descendants, preventing them from ruling on David’s throne
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:24-30 makes clear that God swears no descendant of Coniah will prosper ruling in Judah, marking a divinely imposed end to that line’s kingship.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine communication and human response is illustrated in Jeremiah 22:21?
options: God’s repeated calls are often rejected, showing human stubbornness against divine will
God’s voice is always ignored and ineffective
Human obedience is guaranteed regardless of divine warnings
God only speaks once and never repeats warnings
questions.correctAnswer: God’s repeated calls are often rejected, showing human stubbornness against divine will
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:21 states that God spoke during prosperity but was not heard, indicating a pattern of disobedience from youth, emphasizing human resistance to divine communication.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Jeremiah 22:22 particularly reveal in the context of judgment?
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:22 speaks of the wind eating up pastors and lovers going into captivity as a just consequence of wickedness, highlighting God’s attribute of justice.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 22:15-16 theologically contrast the reigns of kings concerning divine approval?
options: Divine approval is tied to righteous judgment and care for the needy, not to wealth or luxury
Kingship is confirmed by wealth and luxury alone
Divine approval depends on military conquest
Righteousness is irrelevant to God’s acceptance of kings
questions.correctAnswer: Divine approval is tied to righteous judgment and care for the needy, not to wealth or luxury
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:15-16 contrasts the king who closes himself in cedar with his father who did justice and judged the poor, indicating God’s approval depends on righteousness, not opulence.

questions.question: What theological theme is developed by Jeremiah 22:4 regarding obedience and royal succession?
options: Obedience to God’s commands ensures continuity of Davidic kingship and blessing
Royal succession is independent of divine commands
Kingship is maintained through military strength alone
Obedience guarantees immediate political prosperity without conditions
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to God’s commands ensures continuity of Davidic kingship and blessing
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 22:4 promises that if the king obeys, kings and their people will continue to enter the house of David’s throne, linking obedience with covenantal blessing and succession.
